title: Claim Version
description: One L1 claim version — one record on the canonical L1 JSONL surface (spec §5 'L1 — Claim Store'): "L1 is a canonical, append-only JSONL store. Each line is a claim version." The field set below is the spec §6 claim version plus the record-envelope fields the reference implementation carries: the forget-specific fields, the demotion/release warrants, and the optional extraction materialization block (`semantic`). The required field set applies to all versions (active and forgotten). Forgotten versions inherit non-content metadata from the prior active version; the content field is only required when state is active. Forgotten versions add additional required fields per the if/then below.

content.description: The assertion text. Required when state=active. Omitted when state=forgotten (the canonical snapshot lives in the L2 tombstone).

author.description: Voice/body ownership. User-authored bodies are agent-immutable.

epistemic_owner.description: Ownership of confidence, epistemic tag, epistemic relations, and lifecycle. User-owned claims are agent-immutable.

fingerprint.description: Stable identity over normalized content, scope, and claim_type. Preserved across all versions.

derived_from.description: ObservationIds underlying this claim. Agents may extend this only while epistemic_owner=agent; protected-claim corroboration requires user REVISE.

relations.description: Inherited from prior version when version > 1 unless explicitly changed.

created_at.description: Claim's original birth. Equal across all versions of the same claim_id.

version_at.description: This version's commit timestamp. Used by as-of queries.

supersedes.description: Prior version number this one supersedes. Required for version > 1.

endorsement_source.description: PageId that triggered the endorsement cascade producing this version

superseded_by.description: Set on a demoted duplicate (resolved fact match, §1e): the surviving claim that supersedes this one. The claim stays state=active for history and audit; recall eligibility derives from this pointer (status 'superseded').

superseded_at.description: Commit time of the demotion; present whenever superseded_by is.

superseded_by_origin.description: Warrant for the demotion. Absent = the library's mechanical duplicate resolution; 'user' = the user re-picked against this copy (REVISE repick_survivor, protocol v0.5.0).

reinstated_by.description: Audit-only marker on a version that released a demotion: the user reinstated this claim as the recall-eligible copy (REVISE repick_survivor). Never a lifecycle input.

semantic.description: Optional extraction materialization the L1 record writer carries on an active version: the structured meaning the extractor produced (subject, predicate, typed object, valid time) plus the raw pre-reduction epistemic values. It is what makes a record re-materializable — the recall-eligible row (entity name/type, predicate, typed object, valid time, sensitivity, extraction provenance) is derived from this block (ClaimStore.claimVersionVals) — which is why the record envelope enumerates it. It carries no independent epistemic authority: `confidence`/`epistemic_tag` remain the canonical spec §6 values (spec §6 -> 'Implementation note'), nothing in it is required, and a version that omits the block is fully conformant (records written before v0.6 do). Bound types are the writers' declared input contract, not policy: the block is enumerated to the shape the reference writers emit, so that a record the implementation appends validates against the contract it publishes (kanban t_229601e4, ADR-0011). Not a wire field: no protocol request or response carries it.

subject_name.description: Resolved subject entity name (the derived row's `subject_name`).

subject_type.description: Subject entity type (`organization`, `person`, `tool`, `concept`, ...). The record writer defaults it to `concept` when the subject entity is unknown.

value.description: The extracted value. A `date` carries the date as extracted (`2027-01-15`), not a normalised timestamp. Expressed as `anyOf` of single types (not a union `type` array) because the published schemas must compile under AJV strict mode, which rejects union types without `allowUnionTypes`.

t_valid_from.description: Valid-time start the extractor resolved. `state: known` = read from the source; `inferred` = derived, with `basis` naming the rule; `null` = open/unknown.

anyOf.description: A date-time string the extractor passed through without normalising (the LLM extraction path copies the model's `validity.from`, which can be a date without a time). ISO 8601 is the convention; the domain is stated in prose, not as a format requirement, because this value is pass-through extraction output and a format bound would reject a record the writer produced.

t_valid_to.description: Valid-time end the extractor resolved; `state: null` with `value: null` means still open.

anyOf.description: Pass-through extraction output, as for `t_valid_from.value`: the LLM path copies the model's `validity.to`.

extracted_epistemic.description: The extractor's epistemic label BEFORE the canonical reduction (`epistemicToTag`). The canonical value stays `epistemic_tag`; an autonomous claim is bounded to `inference`/`low` on the admitted fields even when the extraction was better (spec §6).

extracted_confidence.description: The extractor's numeric confidence BEFORE bucketing (`confidenceToBucket`); the canonical value stays `confidence`. The declared domain is 0..1 and the `reflect.auto` path clamps to it, but the record writer copies the caller's number verbatim — so the domain is stated here as prose, not as a JSON Schema bound: a bound would reject a record the writer produced, which is the defect this block's enumeration closes.

sensitive.description: Sensitivity flag the extractor set; drives the derived row's `sensitive` column.

then.description: Forgotten versions add forget-specific fields; the core required field set above still applies (metadata is inherited from prior active version).
